::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Define a new evironment by an existed environment, with its optional argument](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/16317/define-a-new-evironment-by-an-existed-environment-with-its-optional-argument), asked by [Stufazi Hoqckt](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/5006/stufazi-hoqckt) on TeX Stack Exchange (2011-04-21; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> Suppose there is an existed environment say, `existedenv`, with an optional argument, that is, 
>
> ```latex
> \begin{existedenv}[argument]
> ....
> \end{existedenv}
> ```
>
> I want to define a new environment, say, `myenv`, which is a copy of `existedenv`, that is,
>
> ```latex
> \begin{myenv}[argument]
> ....
> \end{myenv}
> ```
>
> behavior is exactly like
>
> ```latex
> \begin{existedenv}[argument]
> ....
> \end{existedenv}
> ```
>
> How to write the code?
:::

If you don't want to do anything to the optional argument of `myenv` you can write it without the argument and let `existingenv` take care of it:

```latex
\newenvironment{myenv}{
  % stuff of your own...
  \existingenv
}{
  \endexistingenv
}
```

Then `\begin{myenv}[foo]` will expand to `\begin{existingenv}[foo]` before `foo` is expanded.  

But if this is all you want to do you might consider using some the macros in the [`etoolbox`](http://ctan.org/pkg/etoolbox) package to just patch the environment.  For instance,

```latex
\pretocmd{\A}{stuff of your own}{}{}
```

will just insert the code you want before the begin-code of `A`.
